title: Now Let Our Voices Join
description: Now Let Our Voices Join in Tonic Solfa to ST. BRIDE, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 590, “The Pilgrim's Hymn”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Now let our voi-ces join, To form one plea-sant song: Ye pil-grims in God's ho-ly way, With mu-sic pass a-long!

lines: Ye pilgrims in God's holy way,
No lurking snares to entrap our feet,
The sun of hope shines on our path,
To Him who leads the wanderers on,
And cheers them with His grace.
Teach all their kings Thy ways;
That earth's full choir the notes may swell,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to ST. BRIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
